steps.label: Where they lie
steps.why: Retro means behind, so the answer is about the position of the organ with respect to the peritoneal lining.
common_mistakes: Writing that such an organ has no peritoneum at all. It is covered on the ventral side only.
steps.memory_tip: Retro means behind: the organ sits behind the peritoneum, so only its front face is covered.
steps.margin_note: Say where the organ sits and how much of it the peritoneum covers. Two lines.

steps.label: The name and the example
steps.why: The term is taught through the kidney, so the named example is what the examiner reads first.
common_mistakes: Giving no example. The kidney is the standard example and carries the second mark.
steps.memory_tip: Kidneys lie against the back wall, so the peritoneum can only reach their front face.
steps.margin_note: Name the retroperitoneum and give the kidney as the example.
